cvEn:
Prosper (Peri) Toito, eldest son of Denise and Efraim, was born on 22 Av 5743 (1 August 1983) at Ha'Emek Hospital in Afula. He is the brother of Netanel, Avishai and Dorin.

Peri grew up and was educated in Upper Nazareth. He attended the "Narkisim" and "Egoz" kindergartens and started first grade at the "Hermon" elementary school. He continued his studies at the junior high and high school of the "Orot Alon" comprehensive school, where he was among the graduates of the class of 2001 (5761).

Peri was a prominent figure among his fellow students, known for his strong visual memory, his organizational skills and his readiness to help others. He devoted many hours to "Youth Advancement", an organization whose purpose is to advance young people in Upper Nazareth and prevent them from sliding into drugs, and he found great success and satisfaction in it. In his quiet, grounded and modest way, he was always ready to help his parents, his teachers, his friends and anyone in need of assistance. A true angel, with a pure soul.

Peri was big in stature, but soft and sensitive inside. Integrity, honesty and caring simply flowed from him. His face was like an open book that invited everyone to read it and turn to him for help, and the joy of life radiated from him constantly. His friends called him "Abba Peri" because he always looked out for everyone, supported them and was a listening ear. They say Peri was the "glue" that held them all together, the psychologist who advised and solved every problem, and the most grown-up of them all, who made sure everything ran smoothly.

Peri set himself many goals and always managed to achieve them, despite the difficulties in his path. He made sure to pass this legacy on to his friends, demanding that they work to achieve their own aims. For him, success was defined as the success of his friends and of those around him, together with his own; his personal success alone meant nothing to him.

Peri aspired to greatness. He spoke of studying law after his military service and was determined to be a source of pride to his parents and family. Although his life was so short, he used every moment of his time for action, for giving, and for fulfilling his many dreams. He completed his high school studies with great success and with a full matriculation certificate.

On 9 July 2001 Peri enlisted in the IDF. After completing basic training (Tironut 02) with distinction, he began officer-cadet studies at the Ort Megiddo College in Karmiel, where he completed his studies with distinction and was certified as a communications and cinema technician. In the summer of 2003 he returned to wearing the uniform and went on a course for logistics non-commissioned officers in the Logistics Corps. He stood out for his command abilities, and only a few hours before his death he learned that he had been assigned to the commanders' course he had been waiting for for a long time.

Peri's final project in the film track of the college was a film he directed called "There Is Life After Death", about a soldier killed in a terror attack in Wadi Ara, and about coping with bereavement and loss. By a cruel twist of fate, three months after completing work on the film, Peri was murdered in a bombing attack at Tzrifin.

Peri was taken from us at the height of his life on 12 Elul 5763 (9 September 2003), when he was sent to guard the hitchhiking post at Tzrifin. It was 17:30 when he went out to carry out his duty. At 17:40 a suicide bomber from Hamas arrived at the site, wearing an explosive belt and carrying a bag of metal shrapnel, and detonated himself among the many soldiers and civilians standing at the hitchhiking post. The force of the explosion collapsed the structure, which was completely destroyed. Peri, mortally wounded, was rushed to hospital, but died on the operating table.

Eight other soldiers were killed in the attack along with Peri: Captain Yael Kafir, Master Sergeant Yaakov Ben-Shabbat, Chief Warrant Officer Chaim Alfasi, Sergeant Liron Sibuni, Sergeant Yonatan Peleg, Sergeant Efrat Schwartzman, Corporal Mazi Gargo and Corporal Felix Nikolaichuk. Dozens of people were wounded in the attack, most of them seriously.

Peri's last request, just before they arrived at the hitchhiking post, was to hear the song "Young Forever". And indeed, Peri, twenty years old when he fell, remains young forever. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery in Upper Nazareth. He is survived by his parents, two brothers and a sister. After his death he was posthumously promoted to Corporal.

His parents inscribed the following words on his headstone: "He fought like a lion and fell like a young hero. Peri! Your memory will never fade from our hearts, forever."

In a letter of condolence to the bereaved family, Colonel Tzvika Ganon, commander of Training Base 6, wrote: "Peri completed his initial training in my unit, the Training Base of the Logistics Corps, Training Base 6. Even while on the course, Peri demonstrated high personal abilities and a will to succeed. Thanks to all of these, he served as a model and an example both socially and in command, and that is why he was assigned to an instructional role in my unit. Sadly, a cruel hand cut short his life before its time. Training Base 6 bows its head in sorrow at the loss of Peri, who left a deep mark, in such a short time, on many of his team members and on his course commanders. ... Today it is clear to me where he grew up and what values he received during his very short years. Values of love of the Land of Israel, values of respect for human beings, values of giving, of love and of friendship. His memory will be kept safe in our hearts forever."

Peri's family received many other letters, as well as poems written in his memory.

His cousin Reut Toito wrote: "Her soul crumbled and her heart turned cold as ice / When they told her he was dead she looked at the moon / She filled the darkness with a sea of tears / And made even the stars weep / She can no longer live with the pain / When they took away her son, her heart burned / And everyone knows he will not return and she will not be happy / The weeping is bitter, and only the stars say otherwise // They whisper a prayer, they whisper love / Trying to help her find her son / In skies so blue, in a night so cold / She lost her son on a cruel day // Her eyes lost their spark without mercy / And she was left alone, since her son had no life left / The war was hard and she weeps / Looking at the sun - the sun that has already gone / Asking for his soul back, for his smile / How the heart burned, how he was lost in a tangled maze / And the tears fall again, heavily and sorrowfully / And the stars try to press upon her and widen the gap // They whisper a prayer, they whisper love / Trying to help her find her son / In skies so blue, in a night so cold / She lost her son on a cruel day."

Boris Brodsky, Peri's teacher at the "Orot Alon" school, wrote: "No more! Peri's death stunned his classmates and the entire 'Orot Alon' family. Peri was seen as a mature person, ready to help anyone who asked. The values of respect, equality and integrity in which he was raised found expression in his deeds. Peri worked, both openly and in secret, to bring boys back onto the straight path. The success of those around him mattered more to him than his own. Peri excelled in the communications track and was a source of pride to the school and to his family when he was accepted into the officer-cadet program at the Ort college in Karmiel and completed his studies with distinction. Peri, we will miss you today, we will miss you in the future, and your image will always be engraved in our hearts."

Inbar, one of Peri's female friends, wrote: "... Here I stand, stunned, frightened, searching for the words to describe what is inside. Everyone says, 'The beginning is the hardest', but that is not true. The beginning is not remembered, it is hazy, it seems unreal. The continuation is the hard part, suddenly you discover that this is not a dream, that it is a nightmare, a real nightmare that we have to face every day that passes. ...

Peri... you are the leader and so you will remain forever. You were the wisest among us, the educated one, the funny one, the talented one... the one who always cared about success. You always knew everything first, and so death too, unfortunately! You planted all your goodness in us, each of us has something of you in them. We promise to keep this alive forever, and with us, Peri, you will remain forever and ever."

Yasmin, another friend, wrote: "Things I did not get to say: Peri! I never thought our time was so short, that the moment we would part would be so close, so many things we postponed, that we said 'tomorrow', which never came. You were a friend and a brother to me, you supported, helped and shared, you were like a caring father to me. I remember days and nights of laughter and tears, nerves, joy and shared pain: after all, every problem of mine became yours, and every worry of yours was awakened in me too. You were our glue, you always cared for our unity, we all relied on you with our eyes closed, and you, of course, never disappointed. Your devotion to the goal always amazed me, the desire to go far and the efforts of great worth. Even in the thicket of uncertainty you walked with your head held high, like a guide, you knew how to extricate yourself from every trouble, always in a calculated and honest way. ... As a hero you fell, Peri, as a leader, always thinking of others, listening to the voice of your heart and to the values you grew up on and fell for.
How empty our world is in your absence, in the absence of a person whose presence filled the whole world.
Peri! Your memory will stay with me, with us, forever, and your death is engraved in our hearts, shattered into shards, and in our souls, split in two, because when you left us, something in us died, and something stayed with you. ... I love you and always will."

Eliko, a friend, wrote: "... one after another, people came up to eulogize you, each found for himself the most beautiful words in his dictionary, each one praised and extolled you.
Peri, there are people who are praised when they are killed. But you were praised even when you were alive. Now you are in heaven, among all the angels, under the wings of the Shechinah, and we are still here on earth, among good and bad people.
My brother, I wanted to ask you to watch over us all from above, and to give us the strength to be strong and united, to help us reach where you always wanted to go. ... Your body is not with us, but you remain in our hearts, with us and in our dreams, forever."

Peri's younger sister Dorin said farewell to him in the song "You Can't Stop Me": You are crying / and cannot stop / the tears. / You laugh and cannot / cry / You are sad inside / longing... // You are the best of all / and there is my love in you / because there is in you the feeling of God / You gave me everything / You are beloved... // We are all alive now / only you are in the painful place / in my heart / and there are feelings that cannot be / prevented / because my love lasts forever..."
